title: Buying a Flat? Here’s What ‘No EMI Till Possession’ Actually Means

faq.a: A subvention scheme is another name for a "no EMI till possession" scheme. It's a tripartite agreement where the builder pays the interest on your home loan during the construction period, giving you a payment holiday until you receive possession of the property.

faq.q: Is 'no EMI till possession' truly interest-free?
faq.a: No, it is not interest-free. Interest is still accruing on your home loan. It's just that the builder is undertaking to pay that interest component on your behalf for a specified period. You are still the borrower, and the loan is in your name.

faq.q: What happens if the builder defaults on payments?
faq.a: If the builder defaults on paying the interest, the legal liability falls entirely on you, the homebuyer. The bank will demand payments from you, and your CIBIL score will be negatively impacted if you fail to pay.

faq.q: Can I claim tax benefits on the interest paid by the builder?
faq.a: Yes, the interest paid by the builder on your behalf during the pre-possession period (pre-construction interest) can be claimed as a deduction under Section 24(b) of the Income Tax Act. However, this deduction can only be claimed in five equal annual instalments starting from the financial year of possession, subject to the overall limit of ₹2 lakh for self-occupied property.

faq.q: Has the RBI banned these schemes?
faq.a: The RBI has not issued an outright ban on all subvention schemes. However, it has issued strict warnings and guidelines to banks, discouraging pure subvention schemes where builders receive large upfront disbursements without linking them to construction progress. Banks are advised to exercise due diligence and ensure disbursements are commensurate with the actual stages of construction.

faq.q: What are the main risks for homebuyers?
faq.a: The primary risks include project delays (leading to you paying both rent and EMIs), builder defaults (impacting your CIBIL score), inflated property prices, and limited loan flexibility.

faq.q: Should NRIs consider 'no EMI till possession' schemes?
faq.a: NRIs face similar risks to resident Indians, if not more, due to distance and potential difficulties in monitoring project progress or resolving disputes. While the temporary relief might seem attractive, the inherent risks of project delays and builder defaults make it a high-risk proposition that requires even greater due diligence.
